comparison: Perfect agreement on overall conclusions (C11, C79, C83, C91). Both evaluations support the integrative conclusions about GSDMD's role in psoriasis involving neutrophils. OpenEval notes C91 regarding therapeutic insights is somewhat speculative, while peer reviewers accepted the overall conclusion without challenge.

Both address neutrophil resistance to pyroptosis (C81, C82, C97). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the mechanistic connection to psoriasis is inferential and not directly tested. Peer reviewers rated as SUPPORTED without challenging the interpretation, accepting it as supporting context.

Perfect agreement on dimethyl fumarate context (C84, C85). Both evaluations support these claims as appropriate literature citations providing translational context, though both note these represent prior knowledge rather than novel findings from the study.

Strong agreement on neutrophil-specific conditional knockout findings (C8-C10, C53-C56, C58-C59, C61, C78). Both support the evidence. OpenEval includes C60 (neutrophil depletion) while peer review explicitly mentions it. Peer review notes initial concerns about other cell types were sufficiently addressed.

Strong agreement on global GSDMD knockout phenotype (C7, C38-C43, C76-C77). Both evaluations support the evidence showing phenotypic improvement across multiple measures. Peer reviewers described evidence as 'solid' and having 'potential to unravel the new role of neutrophils.'

Strong agreement on neutrophil-specific GSDMD expression and pyroptosis (C3, C4, C47-C49, C51-C52). Both support the evidence from single-cell transcriptomics and immunostaining. OpenEval includes additional claims (C6, C44-C46, C64) not explicitly mentioned in peer review but implicitly accepted.

Divergent evaluations on mechanistic interpretation of single-cell data (C65-C68). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting mechanistic interpretations are speculative without direct functional validation. Peer reviewers rated as SUPPORTED, accepting the cell-type specific expression patterns without challenge.

Divergent evaluations on neutrophil-derived cytokine effects (C80, C98). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN within R7, noting the mechanistic connection is speculative without direct functional testing. Peer reviewers rated as SUPPORTED in separate result R8, accepting the mechanistic framework without concerns.

Both address elevated GSDMD expression in psoriasis (C1, C2, C5, C33). Both support the findings. OpenEval includes additional claims (C35-C37) about cleaved fragments and validation data. Peer review focuses on correlative RNA-seq and expression data (C1, C2, C5, C6, C33, C44-C46).

Both address the interpretation that neutrophil-specific deletion has less pronounced effects than global deletion (C57). Both support this interpretation. OpenEval includes C60 (neutrophil depletion) while peer review includes C87 (S100a8 expression specificity). Peer review notes initial concerns were sufficiently addressed.

OpenEval evaluated validation of conditional knockout approach (C50, C86-C87, C96) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding standalone peer review evaluation found, though C87 appears in peer R5 and the approach was implicitly accepted in peer R4.

OpenEval evaluated background knowledge about psoriasis epidemiology and pathogenesis (C12-C23, C88-C89, C92-C94) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not separately evaluate background claims.

OpenEval evaluated established pyroptosis mechanism background (C24-C32, C90) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not separately evaluate background mechanistic knowledge.

OpenEval evaluated prior literature and knowledge gap identification (C33-C34, C74-C75, C95) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though C33 appears in peer R1 as part of expression data evaluation.

OpenEval evaluated broader context about pyroptosis in other diseases (C69-C73) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not separately evaluate contextual background claims.

OpenEval evaluated established background knowledge about neutrophils and pyroptosis (C62-C63) as SUPPORTED, noting these represent prior literature rather than novel findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
